To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have calculated the 4-loop corrections to the second and the third moments for vector, axial-vector, and scalar quark-current correlators and that we have calculated 4-loop corrections for the third and the fourth moments of the pseudo-scalar quark current correlator using the Ward identity.
we have developed new techniques for calculating multi-loop Feynman integrals and applied them to the calculation of low-energy moments of heavy-quark current correlators.
we have obtained the first four-loop calculation of the second moment of the vector, axial-vector, and scalar quark-current correlators.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the calculation of multi loop integrals, their application to the calculation of the low-energy moments of heavy-quark current correlators and their use to determine the charm- and the bottom-quark mass.
the calculation of the four-loop contributions to low-energy moments of current-current correlators.
the calculation of the perturbative QCD corrections to the moments of current-current correlators in the limit of large quark mass, where the heavy quark effective theory (HQET) can be applied.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the charm-quark mass and the running strong coupling constant at the charm-quark scale have been determined with a precision that is comparable to the theoretical uncertainties in the determination of the bottom-quark mass and coupling constant.

the four-loop results are not yet needed in order to determine the charm quark and the strong coupling with the present accuracy of the lattice data, but that they will be necessary to improve the determination in the future, in particular when the lattice simulations will reach a higher accuracy.
we are not yet at a stage where the theoretical uncertainty can be quantitatively assessed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the four-loop corrections are small compared to the three-loop results and the experimental errors, so that the three-loop results are sufficient to obtain the quark masses from the moments of current correlators.
the charm-quark mass is determined to a precision of 0.3 % from the moments, and that the bottom-quark mass is known to a precision of about 0.1 %.
we have calculated the four-loop correction for all the moments up to order m 3 q, and that these results are now available in the public domain.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the four-loop results for the second and third moments in the low energy expansions of the vector, axial-vector, pseudo-scalar and scalar quark currents are sufficiently accurate to be used for the analysis of experimental data.
the four-loop contributions to moments of the current correlators are small, but not negligible.
the four-loop contributions to the low-energy moments are numerically large and that the convergence of the low-energy expansion is slow.
